images.filename: Riverside path and Northern Spire, Sunderland (geograph 5963579).jpg
images.caption:
This path along the north bank of the River Wear is for use by pedestrians and cyclists. It forms part of the C2C cycle route across northern England, from the Cumbrian coast to the North Sea. The C2C is part of the National Cycle Network.
On the approach to Sunderland, cyclists are now greeted by this sight of the Northern Spire, which was completed in 2018.

images.filename: Sunderland station, with Newcastle - Middlesbrough express geograph-2848430-by-Ben-Brooksbank.jpg
images.caption:
Sunderland station, with Newcastle - Middlesbrough express.
View westward, towards Newcastle: ex-NER 'Coast' main line: Newcastle - Sunderland - West Hartlepool - Stockton and the South. The train is headed by a Gresley B16/2 rebuild (1/40) of a Raven B16/1 No.846 built 3/20, renumered in 1946 No. 1406, then 61475 in 1949 by BR, withdrawn 4/63. The station was badly damaged by enemy action in 1943 and was already re-roofed in 1953, rebuilt in 1965.

images.caption:
Opened in 1879 by the North Eastern Railway, this station replaced numerous smaller termini that had existed around the town centre.
View north at the forecourt, as rebuilt in 2023. The platforms are underneath but until the Second World War, there was an overall roof where the block of buildings to the left of the station entrance now are. War damage to this was never repaired, it was removed and eventually the whole station area was built over, making the platform area distinctly gloomy. The building of this multi-million pound southern entrance has not changed this.
